{{Commons category|Decahedra}}

In [[geometry]], a '''decahedron''' is a [[polyhedron]] with ten [[Face (geometry)|faces]]. There are 32300 [[topology|topologically]] distinct decahedra,<ref>Gerard Michon: [http://www.numericana.com/data/polyhedra.htm Counting Polyhedra]</ref><ref>{{cite OEIS|A000944}}</ref> and none are regular, so this name does not identify a specific type of polyhedron except for the number of faces.

Some decahedra have regular faces:

* [[Octagonal prism]] (uniform 8-[[Prism (geometry)|prism]])
* [[Square antiprism]] (uniform 4-[[antiprism]])
* [[Square cupola]] ([[Johnson solid]] 4)
* [[Pentagonal bipyramid]] (Johnson solid 13, 5-[[bipyramid]])
* [[Augmented pentagonal prism]] (Johnson solid 52)
* [[Augmented tridiminished icosahedron]] (Johnson solid 64)

Decahedra with irregular faces include:

* [[Pentagonal trapezohedron]] (5-[[trapezohedron]], antiprism dual){{snd}} often used as a [[dice|die]] in [[role playing games]], known as a '''d10'''
* [[Truncated square trapezohedron]]
* [[Enneagon]]al pyramid (9-[[Pyramid (geometry)|pyramid]])
* [[Ten of diamonds decahedron]] - a space-filling polyhedron with D<sub>2d</sub> symmetry
* [[Chamfer (geometry)|Chamfered tetrahedron]]
* [[Square bifrustum]]
